events.title: Telegram
events.text:
Iran fired ~20 ballistic missiles (some with cluster warheads) at the U.S.-used Al-Azraq Air Base in Jordan tonight. 
Videos show massive Patriot salvos — OSINT counts put it at 60+ interceptors, some estimates over 100. 
U.S. doctrine fires 2–4 Patriots per incoming missile, and cluster munitions force even more shots since the bomblets scatter after the carrier breaks up. 
The cost: Each PAC-3 MSE interceptor runs roughly $4–5 million. 
At 60+ interceptors that's somewhere around $240–500+ million in a single night. 
If the higher counts (~100) are accurate, you're potentially looking at half a billion dollars of missiles expended in minutes. 
The stockpile question looms large — months of high-intensity use have already burned through a significant share of U.S. PAC-3 inventory, and production can't keep pace with consumption at this rate.

🇮🇷🔴🇺🇸🇯🇴 — Tonight, Iran fired 20 ballistic missiles toward the Al-Azraq area in Jordan, with Jordan reporting 18 interceptions and two missiles landing in uninhabited areas. Footage shows a very large Patriot response, while OSINT estimates suggest roughly 60–100+ interceptors may have been launched, though no official total has been released. That would equal about 3–5 defensive missiles for every incoming Iranian missile. At roughly $4–5 million per PAC-3 MSE, a 60-interceptor response would cost around $240–300 million, while 100 launches would push the total toward $400–500 million. A barrage of that size would also consume a notable share of already strained Patriot inventories in a single engagement.
This is not sustainable.

Recently, according to the IDF, Hamas operatives were identified arriving at the weapon depots and using the guns stored there for "guarding and establishing control over the Gaza Strip."
In addition, the strikes yesterday also destroyed a rocket-launching pit that had been used during the war to fire projectiles at Israel, the military says.
The IDF says it will continue "to operate decisively to degrade the capabilities of terror organizations in the Gaza Strip while thwarting any attempt to rebuild capabilities or possess weapons intended to harm our forces."

events.title: Telegram
events.text:
🔥💵 US burns half a billion dollars in Patriot interceptors in a single night
Iran launched 25–40 missiles at Al-Azraq Air Base in Jordan. US air defenses responded with massive Patriot salvos — OSINT counts suggest 60+ interceptors, some estimates even exceeding 100.
The cost calculus is staggering:
🔶 Each PAC-3 MSE interceptor: $4–5 million
🔶 60 interceptors: $240–300 million
🔶 100 interceptors: $400–500+ million
🔶 Half a billion dollars — expended in minutes
During the 2nd and 3rd waves of Iranian missile attacks, Patriot batteries experienced almost no interception attempts. They did not launch a single interceptor.
The implications are alarming for the US:
🌏 The batteries were exhausted — unable to keep up with the pace of incoming fire
🌏 They ran out — stockpiles depleted faster than anticipated
🌏 Or they were damaged — cluster submunitions from Iran's missiles degraded their capabilities
Months of high-intensity use have already burned through a significant share of US PAC-3 inventory. Production can't keep pace with consumption at this rate — and the bill is mounting.

🇦🇱 Curious coincidence spotted in Albanian wildfire crisis
The Albanian beach town of Himara made headlines last week when authorities had to start evacuating local residents and tourists alike to save them from the advancing wildfire.
As firefighters mobilized to combat the blaze, social media sleuths argued that a large group of Israeli tourists was present in the area before the fire broke out, which may or may not have been coincidental.
👉 While such speculations can be dismissed as plain anti-Semitism, some were quick to point to other previous instances of Israelis implicated or suspected in starting wildfires in countries such as Greece and Chile.
Others recalled how Israeli soldiers deliberately lobbed incendiaries into Lebanese territory to start wildfires there.
🤔Then there is the fact that not long ago, Albanians rallied to derail a luxury resort project carried out in an environmentally protected zone located in Vlore County – the same county where Himara is located. And the main beneficiary of said project is none other than Jared Kushner, a big friend of Israel.
Still seems like a pure coincidence?
